Interface Platform

All Known Implementing Classes:
FakePlatform
public interface Platform
The platform the JVM runs on: its operating system and the directories applications use on it.

Use current() to get the platform of the running JVM. Code that receives a Platform instead of calling current() itself can be tested against any platform.

At most one of isLinux(), isMacOS() and isWindows() is true. On other Unix-like systems, such as FreeBSD, all three are false, and the directories follow the XDG Base Directory Specification, as on Linux.

    • applicationDirectories

      default ApplicationDirectories applicationDirectories(String application)
      Returns the directories of an application, named by its name alone.
      • Linux, Unix: ~/.config/app, ~/.local/share/app, ~/.local/state/app, ~/.cache/app and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/app, under the base directories, where app is the name in lower case with spaces replaced by -
      • macOS: config, data and state in ~/Library/Application Support/App, and ~/Library/Caches/App
      • Windows: config and data in %APPDATA%\App, state and cache in %LOCALAPPDATA%\App
      Parameters:
      application - the name of the application, such as Quuz
      Returns:
      the directories of the application
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the name is blank, . or .., starts or ends with whitespace, or contains a control character or any of / \ : < > " | ? *, which some platform forbids in a file name
      Since:
      0.1.1

    • applicationDirectories

      default ApplicationDirectories applicationDirectories(String vendor, String application)
      Returns the directories of an application, named by its vendor and its name. Only Windows uses the vendor, as a directory above the application's: %APPDATA%\Vendor\App and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Vendor\App. Otherwise, the directories are those of applicationDirectories(String).
      Parameters:
      vendor - the name of the organization or person that makes the application, such as bar
      application - the name of the application, such as Quuz
      Returns:
      the directories of the application
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a name is blank, . or .., starts or ends with whitespace, or contains a control character or any of / \ : < > " | ? *, which some platform forbids in a file name
      Since:
      0.1.1

    • applicationDirectories

      default ApplicationDirectories applicationDirectories(String qualifier, String vendor, String application)
      Returns the directories of an application, named by its vendor's qualifier, its vendor and its name. Only macOS uses the qualifier: its directories are named after the bundle-style identifier qualifier.vendor.App, such as ~/Library/Application Support/foo.bar.Quuz, with spaces replaced by -. Otherwise, the directories are those of applicationDirectories(String, String).
      Parameters:
      qualifier - the top-level domain of the vendor, such as foo
      vendor - the name of the organization or person that makes the application, such as bar
      application - the name of the application, such as Quuz
      Returns:
      the directories of the application
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a name is blank, . or .., starts or ends with whitespace, or contains a control character or any of / \ : < > " | ? *, which some platform forbids in a file name
      Since:
      0.1.1
